what: Inputs of the Place page's pencil. Every value is either sourced (with its document and section) or an example to replace with your own; the card labels each.

hud_mtsp.title: HUD FY2026 Multifamily Tax Subsidy Project income limits, Pittsburgh HMFA (HUD User API)

hacp_ua.title: Housing Authority of the City of Pittsburgh, 2026 HCV Utility Allowance Schedule (effective 2026-01-01)

obbba.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1, 119th Congress, enacted July 4, 2025), amending IRC §42(h)(4)(B): the 25% bond test

phfa_draft.title: PHFA 2027/2028 draft Qualified Allocation Plan (board-approved for public comment, 2026-07-13; not adopted)

phfa_uw.title: PHFA 2025 Underwriting Application, Tab 2 (core application and operating budget instructions)

nine.ref: §42(b)(2): the 9% floor for new buildings not federally subsidized

four.ref: §42(b)(3): the 4% floor for buildings financed with tax-exempt bonds

boost.ref: §42(d)(5)(B): 130% of eligible basis in a QCT or DDA; PHFA §2.6: a state boost needs a waiver for 9% deals and is not available to 4% bond deals

bond_test.ref: Tax-exempt bonds of at least 25% of the aggregate basis of building and land (was 50%), and at least one bond issue after 2025 financing 5% or more of it, for buildings placed in service after 2025 (P.L. 119-21 §70422); confirm with bond counsel

basis_per_home.ref: §3.4 Maximum per unit basis (depreciable costs, no developer fee or acquisition)

credit_cap.ref: §2.4 per project maximums for 9% credits: $1.8M with 60+ affordable homes and at least 51% 2-bedroom or larger, $1.85M supportive housing, $1.7M otherwise

fee.ref: §3.5 developer's fee: 15% of the first $10M of replacement cost (less acquisition), 10% after; 9% caps $2.0M (60+ affordable homes and 51% 2BR+, or supportive) and $1.75M; 4% paid fee cap $2.55M

feasible_gap_share.ref: §3.2.20: any gap, unsecured sources included, must be under 50% of the developer fee

funded_gap_share.ref: Selection criteria D.4.a: a gap under 25% of the developer fee still counts as fully funded

large_homes.ref: §2.4 and §3.5: the higher caps need 60 or more affordable homes

large_2br_share.ref: §2.4 and §3.5: and at least 51% of homes with 2 or more bedrooms

set_aside.ref: §42(g)(1): 20% of homes at 50% AMI, or 40% at 60% AMI, or income averaging (40% of homes, average designation at most 60%, none above 80%)

ua.ref: Low-rise apartment (4 stories or fewer), standard: tenant pays electric heat pump heating, electric cooking, other electric, air conditioning and electric water heating; owner pays water, sewer and trash

hard_per_sf.note: Hard construction cost. Replace with a contractor's estimate

soft_share.note: Design, permits, financing, insurance, legal, reserves

efficiency.note: Halls, stairs and walls take the rest (the zoning card uses the same figure)

opex_per_home.note: Operating cost with property taxes, before reserves

dscr.note: Debt service coverage the lender asks for

price_nine.unit: $ of equity a dollar of credit
price_nine.note: Credit price for 9% credits; ask a syndicator

price_four.unit: $ of equity a dollar of credit

ineligible_share.note: Costs outside eligible basis (permanent loan fees, reserves, marketing)

soft_funds.note: Soft funds applied for or expected, not yet committed: URA, HOME, PennHOMES, Housing Trust Fund. PHFA counts them as gap until committed

state_boost.note: PHFA's state basis boost (9% only, by waiver)

target_yield.note: Yield on cost a market-rate project needs

soft_committed.note: Soft funds committed in writing (award letters)

supportive.note: Supportive housing preference (25% of homes set aside in the Urban pool; caps apply if awarded)

basis_per_home.ref: §3.4.1 and §7.2: no per-home basis limit for 9% (costs reviewed as excessive or not); for 4%, a $400,000-a-home Max Basis test only when the bond test exceeds 35% (not modeled: the pencil assumes 25–35%)

credit_cap.ref: §2.4 per project maximums for 9% credits: $2.0M with 65+ affordable homes and at least 51% 2-bedroom or larger, or awarded in the supportive housing preference; $1.85M otherwise

fee.ref: §5.1–5.3 developer's fee: 15% of the first $10M of replacement cost (less acquisition), 10% after; 9% caps $2.3M (65+ affordable homes and 51% 2BR+), $2.1M (supportive preference), $1.9M otherwise ($2.2M with a Pass-Exceed joint venture, not modeled); 4% paid fee cap the higher of $2.55M and $10,000 a home

feasible_gap_share.ref: §3.4.2: any gap, unsecured sources included, must be under 50% of the developer fee, and no negative cash flow before year 11

funded_gap_share.ref: Adopted selection criteria D.4.a (the draft scores commitment of funds under §4.5.9 instead)

large_homes.ref: §2.4 and §5.2: the higher caps need 65 or more affordable homes

large_2br_share.ref: §2.4 and §5.2: and at least 51% of homes with 2 or more bedrooms

commitment.ref: §4.5.9 commitment of funds: deferred (reinvested) fee under 10% of the fee scores Pass-Exceed, 10–30% Pass-Basic, above 30% fails to score

pools.ref: §2.2.1: a LIHTC-only pool (credits and an amortizing first mortgage only; at least 25% of credits) and a LIHTC + Soft Resources pool (any Agency soft funds: HTF, PennHOMES, PA Affordable Housing Tax Credit proceeds, PHARE, Health for Housing; at most 75%), within the Urban and Suburban/Rural pools; the supportive preference needs 25% of homes set aside in the Urban pool

draft.label: 2027/2028 draft plan
draft.ref: The next 9% round (applications due 2027-02-17) runs under the 2027/2028 plan once adopted; it is a draft until PHFA's board adopts it and the Governor approves

vacancy.ref: Tab 2 line 5: a 5% residential vacancy rate on all projects

reserves_general.ref: Tab 2 line 49: replacement reserve $500 a home a year for general or family

reserves_senior.ref: Tab 2 line 49: $375 a home a year for elderly (55+ and 62+)

dscr.ref: Tab 2 line 55: the mortgage the property can support at 115% debt service coverage

income_trend.ref: Tab 2: income trended at 2% a year

expense_trend.ref: Tab 2: expenses trended at 3% a year

positive_years.ref: Tab 2 and draft §3.4.2: cash flow positive through the first 10 years (no negative cash flow before year 11)

fee_repaid_years.ref: Investor practice; the adopted plan ties 15-year repayment to fee waivers only (§5.4), and the draft drops it: shown, not counted
